text:
The rain lashed against the precinct windows, mirroring the storm raging inside Detective Howard’s chest. It was his last day. The retirement party was scheduled for 8:00 AM, complete with a cake and a speech about loyalty. But at 6:00 AM, a tip had led him to a burner phone in his partner’s locker. The texts were damning: coordinates, times, and a name that matched the victim in the cold case Howard had been obsessed with for three years.

His partner, Marcus, had been his brother in arms for twenty-five years. They had covered each other’s backs in alleyways and boardrooms alike. To report this was to destroy the man who had held Howard’s hand when his wife died, who had bailed him out of jail when he was framed for a crime he didn’t commit. But to ignore it was to betray the badge, the victim, and the very code that had defined Howard’s life.

As Howard stared at the evidence, the phone in his pocket buzzed. It was Marcus. *"Hey partner, ready for the big day? I picked up the coffee. See you in ten."*

The casual tone was a knife in the gut. Howard looked at the clock. Ten minutes. If he waited, he could confront Marcus, maybe find a way to make it go away, or maybe Marcus would run. If he acted now, he would be arresting his best friend before the cake was even cut. The weight of the decision pressed down on him, heavier than his service revolver. He had to choose: the man he loved, or the truth he owed.
